card.name: HCl and hydrochloride in drug names
card.fires_on: The 'Cl' or 'CL' after 'H' (HCl) or the end of 'hydrochloride' following a drug name such as metformin, glipizide or paroxetine. It also fires weakly on a few unrelated words in general text.

modes.label: HCl salt after drug name
modes.description: The 'Cl' piece of 'HCl' right after a drug name, in label text.
modes.example: When such drugs are administered to a patient receiving Glipizide and Metformin H<<Cl>> Tablets, the patient should be closely observed

modes.label: End of hydrochloride
modes.description: The closing 'ide' of the word hydrochloride after a drug name.
modes.example: The risk of hypoglycemia is increased when linagliptin and metformin hydrochlor<<ide>> is used in combination with an insulin secret

modes.label: Stray web-text words
modes.description: Occasional ordinary words in general text, such as 'planet' or 'used', that do not fit the drug pattern.
modes.example: The most expensive cars on the<< planet>> are probably the hydrogen fuel cell test vehicles

card.plain: It lights up on the 'HCl' salt label that follows a drug name like metformin.
